study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Brain Structural Phenotype of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using the Normative Model

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to develop normative models for the weights of NMF factors. A radial basis function (RBF) kernel was used as the covariance function. 10-fold cross-validation was used to assess generalizability.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we developed a normative model by training a GPR on the ABIDE II TD cohort, using age and gender as covariates to predict weights; GPR is a Bayesian nonparametric interpolation method that yields coherent measures of predictive confidence in addition to point estimates; we used Gaussian process regression (GPR) to estimate the normative models of weights
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Shan2022.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling; 1-s2.0-S000632232200052X-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplemental Methods / Gaussian process regression

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The response variable was the weight of each NMF factor derived from gray matter volume (GMV) maps. The GM matrix was decomposed into 6 latent factors and corresponding weights using non-negative matrix factorization. Each factor weight represents the contribution of that spatial pattern to an individual's GMV.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: In each model, the weight of factor was the response variable; we used the weights as the response variable which represent the individual differences in GM volume; The GM matrix was decomposed into six factors and corresponding weights
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Shan2022.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling; 1-s2.0-S000632232200052X-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplemental Methods / Selection of covariates

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and gender (sex) were used as covariates in the normative model to predict the weights of factors. Age was treated as a continuous variable and gender as a categorical variable.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: using age and gender as covariates to predict weights; we chose age and gender as the covariates to define the mapping; In each model, the weight of factor was the response variable, and age and gender were covariates
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Shan2022.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling; 1-s2.0-S000632232200052X-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplemental Methods / Selection of covariates
